question: A tool generates a markdown report and returns a resource block with uri "file:///tmp/report.md" and the report text inline in the resource's "text" field. A developer later assumes the SDK will read the report from that filesystem path if needed again. Is this assumption correct?
options: A) Yes, the SDK automatically re-reads the file at that path whenever the resource is referenced again
B) No, the uri is only a label Claude can reference; the actual content already rode along in the "text" field
C) No, resource blocks are discarded after the turn and cannot be referenced again under any circumstance
D) Yes, but only if the resource block also sets "blob" instead of "text"
correct_answers: B) No, the uri is only a label Claude can reference; the actual content already rode along in the "text" field
explanations: Incorrect. The SDK does not read from the filesystem path in a resource uri; the content must already be included in the block.
Correct. The resource's uri is an identifier or label for Claude to reference; it is not a path the SDK reads from. The actual content travels inline in "text" (or "blob" for binary data).
Incorrect. Resources are not universally discarded; Claude can reference the uri as a label within the conversation, it just isn't backed by a live filesystem read.
Incorrect. Using "blob" changes how binary content is encoded, but it does not cause the SDK to start reading from the filesystem path in "uri".
